correctness.rationale: Zeckendorf uniqueness reduces to nonadjacent subsets. An exact ordered-tuple model over full Pisano periods gives an exact leading term. Single equality and adjacency events respectively yield the doubled-index and adjacent-index first-order corrections; all intersections of at least two distinct events contribute only the next lower order. Dividing by k! yields the stated formula, and partial periods give the unaligned leading limit. The critical finite-cycle constants were recomputed as exact rational numbers and compared to independent integer DP and direct small subset enumerations. The finite checks are corroborative, not proof of the asymptotic.

value.rationale: The 2026 Zeckendorf–Niven progression results leave natural conditional-frequency questions on thin fixed-weight families. The theorem supplies exact, algorithmically computable nonuniform proportions for every fixed weight and modulus, resolves the first finite-cutoff correction using the Fibonacci adjacency identity, and separates fixed-weight prevalence from zero overall natural density. The contrast 5/9, 85/256, 7/27, 1/5 exhibits genuine arithmetic structure not captured by a uniform 1/k heuristic.
